articles.title: [Two Pronged] Fighting an erection problem by sleeping with a woman?
articles.summary: Our letter sender writes, 'I sometimes lose my erection when I do that with a man. I really want to try having sex with a woman, but I’m afraid that I might also lose my erection with her.'

blocks.text: Rappler’s People section runs an advice column by couple Jeremy Baer and clinical psychologist Dr. Margarita Holmes.

Jeremy has a master’s degree in law from Oxford University. A banker of 37 years who worked in three continents, he has been training with Dr. Holmes for the last 10 years as co-lecturer and, occasionally, as co-therapist, especially with clients whose financial concerns intrude into their daily lives.
Together, they have written two books: Love Triangles: Understanding the Macho-Mistress Mentality and Imported Love: Filipino-Foreign Liaisons.
Dear Dr. Holmes and Mr. Baer,
I’m usually more of a bottom/receiver, but sometimes when I’m vers, there are occasions when I receive oral sex or masturbate, and I’ve also tried being the insertive partner during anal sex.
However, I sometimes lose my erection when I do that with a man. I really want to try having sex with a woman, but I’m afraid that I might also lose my erection with her.
Please respect my confession — I genuinely need advice.
– Peter
Dear Peter,
Thank you for your message. You seem to have two issues at work here — the loss of erection and the wish to try sleeping with a woman.

Erectile problems are very common. The causes are varied — substance abuse, typically alcohol or drugs, medication (prescribed or not), depression, anxiety, stress. Often, a new situation or a new partner can cause anxiety that then kills an erection. This can create performance anxiety which subsequently leads to more erection loss. The key is to break the loop.

Firstly, it helps to remember that penetrative sex is not the only type of sex. Touch, oral, kissing, cuddling are also part of the sexual repertoire. Embracing this variety will help avoid performance pressure.
Take careful note of what enhances your erection and what kills it. Indulge the former and avoid the latter, especially alcohol.

Choose your partner with care. You want them to be kind and considerate of your erection issue. Take them into your confidence if you can so that there is patience, not judgment, if there are problems.

Take note of excessive expectations. If you are embarking on something that is outside your normal experience, it is sensible to aim not for Olympic but instead novice standards. If not, you set yourself up for likely failure. It is very helpful too if you can share your inexperience with your partner so that their expectations are also tempered.

As for sleeping with a woman, what has changed your thinking now? There are several possibilities: for example, variety for variety’s sake or trying to express some more confident “you”. Analyzing your past behavior will provide you with a window to the future. Once you understand where you are coming from, it will be much easier to chart a new course.
Wishing you every success on your journey of new discoveries.
– JAF Baer
Dear Peter:

Thank you very much for your letter. I agree very much with almost everything Mr Baer says. However, I believe he is being overly optimistic when he writes: “There are several possibilities (to explain what has changed your mind about sleeping with women) — for example, variety for variety’s sake or trying to express some more confident ‘you.’”
In truth, maybe I am too harsh with Mr Baer. Maybe he was just trying to be kind to you when he said one reason for your possibly sleeping with women is variety for variety’s sake.

I think the reason you want to sleep with a woman now is that you want to find out if it is easier to maintain your erection with a woman than it is with a man… In which case it is very unfair of you to want to use a woman like that.

No, no, no, I am not suggesting you have to be in love with someone before you sleep with them. Indeed, there can even be a different need/lust fulfilled when you have a quickie with someone you hardly know.

But you see, even in this case, you are responding to the actual person you are having sex with. In this case, you are not having sex with the person simply because they fit the correct category (woman as opposed to man). That would be a very cold, and hence unfair, reason to have sex with someone.

At least… if you have not been honest with her to begin with. If you had not told her, in clear and certain terms, that you want to sleep with her mainly because you want to know if you can “get it up” with a woman.

This is the major reason it is best to have sex with someone you have a certain affinity for. No, it does not mean you have to have known them for ages (though that can help). Sometimes you might have met them just that night.

DISCLAIMER: This can only happen if you have impeccable instincts for people and even if you cannot guarantee your penis will remain hard when you try and penetrate, you can be damn sure they will not make you feel bad that you tried.

And trying is what matters most. AND seeking help from the right professional if need be – and that can be anything from a urologist, a psychiatrist or clinical psychologist, and/or a counselor who can help give you a better perspective on what being a top truly means to you and how best to achieve it if you decide it is truly important.
Good luck and wishing you all the very best.
— MG Holmes

articles.title: ‘Serious incident’ at Alberta military base causes deaths and injuries, Canada officials say
articles.summary:
Incident at CFB Wainwright base in Alberta caused a ‘major fire’ that is spreading to the nearby town because of strong winds

People have been killed and injured after an incident at one of…

blocks.text: People have been killed and injured after an incident at one of Canada’s busiest military training bases in Alberta caused a large fire, Canada’s defence minister said Saturday.
“I’m saddened to share that there have been both fatalities and injuries as a result of an incident on the base,” defence minister David McGuinty said at a press conference on Saturday night.

McGuinty described the situation at CFB Wainwright as “active and delicate” with the fire being monitored very closely. “I cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory”, he said at the press conference.

McGuinty did not provide casualty figures or details about what caused the incident. The Canadian Armed Forces and federal, provincial and local authorities were coordinating the emergency response, he said. The nearby community of Wainwright was providing hospital and firefighting support.
In an earlier social media post, prime minister Mark Carney said: “A serious incident creating a major fire has occurred at CFB Wainwright, in Alberta.”
“Our thoughts are with all the brave women and men affected,” he said.

The Municipal District of Wainwright said the fire crossed the base’s fence earlier Saturday and was spreading rapidly due to high winds. Firefighters from multiple jurisdictions were responding, and no evacuation order was in effect.
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith described the fire as “significant and tragic” and said it was affecting many military personnel.

Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, about 180km southeast of Edmonton, is one of Canada’s busiest military training bases, where soldiers prepare for combat operations. It is home to the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, which conducts realistic battlefield exercises, and the 3rd Canadian Division Training Centre, which provides military training.
Canadian Conservative opposition leader Pierre Poilievre said he had spoken with Carney and the defence minister to offer support to those affected by the fire.
“Pray for Wainwright, everyone,” Poilievre said in a social media post. He urged people in the area to follow emergency instructions and keep roads clear for first responders.
Neither Carney nor Smith provided details about what caused the fire or whether anyone was injured.

blocks.text: Published October 18, 2026 10:35am
The Department of Health (DOH) on Sunday warned the public about the harmful health effects of cadmium, a toxic metal found in vape aerosols.
Cadmium can damage the kidneys and bones, while prolonged exposure may increase the risk of cancer, the DOH said in Mao dela Cruz’s Super Radyo dzBB report.
.@DOHgovph, nagbabala laban sa masamang epekto sa kalusugan ng cadmium, na natatagpuan sa aerosol ng vape. | via Mao Dela Cruz https://t.co/q15027pz56— DZBB Super Radyo (@dzbb) October 18, 2026
Aside from cadmium, vape aerosols may contain other harmful chemicals, including benzene, diacetyl, and acrolein.
The DOH urged the public, particularly the youth, to avoid vaping due to its harmful components.
It also backed calls to implement higher taxes on vapes to help make potentially harmful products less affordable and accessible.
Earlier this month, the Philippine Tobacco Harm Reduction Advocates (PHILTRA) said health advocates urged the government to consider higher excise taxes on vape products.
E-liquids are currently taxed differently depending on whether they contain salt nicotine or freebase nicotine.

Meanwhile, the Department of Finance is proposing a unified excise tax of P72.93 per 2 milliliters or 2 grams on e-cigarettes and heated tobacco products, on top of a P150 excise tax per device. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: 'Champi' seen entering PAR at super typhoon strength
articles.summary: The super typhoon may enter PAR at peak strength and will be locally named Rosal.

blocks.text: October 18, 2026 | 10:17am
The relative position of a super typhoon, internationally named Champi, as seen in this satellite rendering as of Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026 at 11:30 a.m.
Windy

MANILA, Philippines — Super Typhoon Champi may enter the Philippine area of responsibility by Tuesday morning or afternoon, October 20, while maintaining its strength, state weather bureau PAGASA said.
In its advisory Sunday morning, PAGASA said the tropical cyclone will be given the local name Rosal once inside PAR.
As of 11 a.m. Sunday, October 18, Champi was estimated 2,090 kilometers east of southeastern Luzon, outside PAR.
The super typhoon had maximum sustained winds of 185 kilometers per hour near the center, gusts of up to 230 kph and a central pressure of 940 hectopascals.
Champi was maintaining its strength while moving westward over the sea near Guam, PAGASA noted.
The cyclone is forecast to move generally west-northwestward and enter PAR by Tuesday morning or afternoon.
Champi is expected to remain a super typhoon as it crosses into PAR before gradually weakening beginning Tuesday after reaching its peak intensity.
PAGASA said the cyclone will continue moving west-northwestward toward Taiwan.

Voters in 161 B.C. municipalities go to the polls to elect their next mayor and council, school board and, in some cases, park board. October 18Surrey candidates weigh new facilities and housing growthAkshay KulkarniSurrey mayor says $360M Vancouver Giants arena will be built on timeThe City of Surrey plans to build a 10,000-seat hockey arena that will be the new home of the WHL's Vancouver Giants. Surrey Mayor Brenda Locke defended the project, and said it would not lead to unnecessary costs for taxpayers while Giants majority owner Ron Toigo says the team will not immediately move to rename itself the Surrey Giants.Surrey's mayoral candidates have promised a range of new community and recreation facilities if elected, including a waterfront district, a conference centre and new pools.Building community infrastructure to serve Surrey's burgeoning population has been a big issue for years, with a 10,000-seat arena the latest major facility to be greenlit — even as the cost of the police transition weighs on the city's budget.The major candidates, however, have different ideas on how they'll balance housing and population growth to go along with those large projects.Locke says she will build on her work in the past, including approving more than 13,800 net new units.Annis and McCallum, meanwhile, are pushing back on the province's push for more dense housing centred around public transit. Annis says infrastructure needs to keep up with growth, while McCallum is pushing for the Crescent Beach and Ocean Park areas to be excluded from provincial housing legislation.Starchuk has promised to build more affordable homes on city land, with priority for family-sized homes.Troy Van Vliet is promising a family housing policy to include targets for two- and three-bedroom homes, while Honveer Randhawa says he would guarantee that building permits for single-family homes and renovations stamped by authorized firms are issued within five business days.

Race to watch: Locke and McCallum face off again in SurreyAkshay KulkarniWho will be the next mayor of Surrey?CBC’s The Early Edition brought together five candidates vying to be mayor of Surrey for two debates: Mike Starchuk with Imagine Surrey, Surrey city councillor Linda Annis, incumbent mayor Brenda Locke, Conservative Party of Surrey candidate Honveer Randhawa and Troy Van Vilet, a Surrey builder and business owner.Much like in Vancouver, former council allies are competing for the mayoral role in Surrey, B.C.'s second-largest city by population and one whose population growth rate led Canada for many years.Incumbent Brenda Locke of Surrey Connect was formerly a councillor under Doug McCallum, the city's mayor between 2018 and 2022 who is now running again with the Safe Surrey Coalition.The pair split in 2019 over McCallum's support for an independent Surrey Police Service (SPS), with Locke preferring to stay with the Surrey RCMP.With that issue now largely in the rearview mirror — the province having ordered the transition to the SPS — Locke and McCallum join a crowded field as they aim for the city's top job once again.Among those on the list are Coun. Linda Annis, who leads the Surrey First slate, and former MLA and councillor Mike Starchuk, leader of the Imagine Surrey slate.Two candidates — Honveer Randhawa of the Conservative Electors Association and Troy Van Vliet of Surrey Now — haven't held elected office before.

Property taxes a key issue in VancouverAkshay KulkarniVancouver Mayor Ken Sim promises tax freeze and community centres if re-electedVancouver Mayor Ken Sim made his final State of the City address for his first term to the Board of Trade on Wednesday, and with it came two big election promises. Justin McElroy reports on what the mayor is putting front and centre in his platform. Sim swept to power with a super-majority in 2022 on the back of a campaign largely focused on public safety.After four years as mayor, Sim is now promising a property tax freeze if an ABC majority is elected, after the 2026 budget featured one, too.All the other major candidates in the race have slammed that move and Sim's promise, with Fry saying the budgeted property tax freeze led to major cutbacks in city services and administration. Fry has promised more accessible, line-item budgets if he's elected.Allam has promised to cap property tax increases to the rate of inflation, while Hardwick is also promising "predictable increases" in line with inflation.Bligh has promised to replace the property tax freeze with increases based on long-term planning.

Race to watch: Vancouver mayoral race features 5 main slatesAkshay KulkarniVancouver’s mayoral field shifts into focusAfter a week where two Vancouver mayoral candidates left the race, voters are getting a clearer sense of the main choices on the ballot next month. As the CBC's Justin McElroy reports, they’re all trying to position themselves in slightly different ways.The leaders of five major political slates are aiming to be mayor of B.C.'s most populous city.They include the incumbent, Ken Sim of ABC Vancouver, and his former chief of staff, Kareem Allam, who is running for the Vancouver Liberals.Two longtime councillors — Pete Fry of the Vancouver Greens, and Rebecca Bligh of Vote Vancouver — are also in the race, as is former councillor Colleen Hardwick of TEAM Vancouver.Bligh was kicked out of ABC Vancouver last year while Hardwick ran for council in 2018 with Sim, who was then the NPA's mayoral candidate.Fry was the only opposition voice in the previous council for a period of time due to councillor vacancies and an ABC super-majority.

What does a local government do?Arden McLeodWhat municipalities can and can’t do in B.C.With municipal and provincial elections going on at the same time, it can be hard to know which promises being made at the local level are realistic, and which ones aren’t. The CBC’s Justin McElroy explains what powers cities actually have.Many major funding and policy decisions sit with the province and its ministries. But Kimberly Speers, who teaches public administration at UVic, says people can feel the impact of local government decisions every day."It's not generally seen as, you know, an exciting part of governing ... but at the same time, my gosh, are those local services so, so important," Speers said.Municipalities like Vancouver tend to spend the most on protective services, such as police, fire, and emergency services.Another big ticket item for municipalities is utilities like water, sewage and waste. Municipalities also oversee parks, recreation and culture centres and how land-use is determined — as well as maintaining sidewalks, roads and public transportation.

Multiple votes to cast in civic electionsArden McLeodElection overload is real in B.C. ahead of 2 back-to-back votesElection overload is real in B.C. with 2 back-to-back votesMunicipal political parties generally don't map neatly onto provincial parties across B.C., and depending on where you live, polling can include elections for bodies like school boards, as well as for mayor and council.In Vancouver, for instance, residents are voting for one mayor, 10 city councillors, seven park board commissioners and nine school board trustees.In provincial elections, on the other hand, voters simply choose one candidate to represent their riding in the legislature.

Record number of advance voters in some municipalitiesAkshay KulkarniA cyclist heading toward an advance voting station in Vancouver. (Nav Rahi/CBC)Vancouver is among many municipalities that saw a record number of residents make use of advance voting opportunities for this election.The city says 103,000 voters cast a ballot over four advance voting days, smashing a record of 65,127 in 2022. Officials also say mail-in voting requests doubled compared to 2022, with 21,000 requests this year.Surrey and Kelowna, among others, also saw high advance voter turnouts.Every municipality was required to provide at least one advance voting day in B.C.That's encouraging because, despite a local government's major impact on voters' lives — given they are usually responsible for day-to-day services like garbage collection, sewage and policing — voter turnout in B.C.'s civic elections are usually lower than provincial and federal elections.In 2022, 29.2 per cent of eligible voters cast a ballot, well below the turnout for the subsequent provincial and federal elections, according to CivicInfoBC.

Where to find election resultsCBC NewsSignage in Vancouver on Oct. 7, the second day of advance voting. (Nav Rahi/CBC)CBC British Columbia has election special coverage starting at 8 p.m. PT, bringing you live results as polls close. You can follow updates through the following:Online: CBC Gem, YouTube and on this page.TV: CBC Television (check your local listings for the channel).Radio: CBC Radio One in Vancouver at 88.1 FM or listen online.If you're looking for live results for these major cities, tap the links below: VancouverSurreyRichmondVictoriaKelownaPrince GeorgeKamloops

It's election night in British Columbia – the 1st of 2Rhianna SchmunkA voting sign in Vancouver on Oct. 7. (Nav Rahi/CBC)British Columbians are choosing their next local representatives on councils, school boards and other regional posts on Saturday, the first of two election days this month.The Union of B.C. Municipalities says more than 3,500 local government candidates are running across 189 local bodies in B.C., which include municipalities and regional districts. CBC's Decision Desk will be closely following the vote count after polls close across most of the province at 8 p.m. local time, and will deliver projections of the results in some of B.C.'s biggest communities, including Kamloops, Kelowna, Richmond, Surrey, Vancouver and Victoria.The overlapping provincial election had many worried about widespread voter confusion. Still, many cities and municipalities reported increased or even record turnout at advance polls, including Vancouver, Richmond, Burnaby, Kamloops, Surrey, Kelowna, Prince George, Cranbrook and View Royal.Voters will cast their ballots again next Saturday for the provincial election.

articles.title: Dubai visa scam leaves hundreds of OFWs in financial, legal woes
articles.summary: Dubai authorities eye Interpol assistance after a massive freelance visa fraud scheme swindled an estimated 400 OFWs

blocks.text: DUBAI, United Arab Emirates – Two alleged scammers have reportedly fled the country after pocketing AED 3.6 million (P61.7 million) from around 400 overseas Filipino workers (OFWs), in what could be the United Arab Emirates’ largest visa fraud case in recent years.

The alleged suspects — Junie Sorsano, a prominent Dubai-based content creator for over a decade, and Ryan Ronel Baco — left the UAE during the first week of September and are now reportedly hiding in the Philippines.
An undetermined number of victims still in the Philippines have also organized to seek help from authorities.
Sorsano serves as the CEO and founder of Trip Expert Business and Marketing Solutions, which opened on May 15, 2025, while Baco operates as the managing director.

The firm offered “legitimate and legal” freelance visa packages priced at AED 9,000 (P154,500) per applicant. The packages bypassed standard Philippine government safeguards, including contract verifications by the Migrant Workers Office (MWO) and the Overseas Employment Certificate (OEC), as well as the UAE-prescribed electronic salary transfer system.
Prior to fleeing, Sorsano and Baco issued a joint public apology in September.
“We ask for your patience and kind consideration while we work through this challenging period,” the statement read.

However, victims reported that the two have been completely unreachable since the statement was released. Furthermore, Trip Expert’s primary corporate office in Deira, Dubai, has been closed due to an alleged failure to pay rent.

Victims noted that a major factor that drew them to the company was the involvement of two popular vloggers, who regularly appeared in advertisements promoting the merits of the freelance visa package.

The digital creators, Abdul Hamid Bandon and Enrico Cardoniga, have strongly denied any involvement in the fraudulent scheme. On the contrary, both said the controversy has severely damaged their vlogging careers.
Cardoniga, acting on legal advice, declined to go on record but disclosed that two major brands have already suspended their partnerships with him.
Meanwhile, Bandon said he is waiting for the situation to “cool down” before speaking extensively. “May mga nagtatanong sa akin (People are asking me),” he said.
Ambrosio Brian Enciso III, Consul General at the Philippine Consulate General (PCG) in Dubai and the Northern Emirates, confirmed that authorities are actively investigating the scheme.
“The Migrant Workers Office (MWO) Dubai, through its retained legal counsel, is providing appropriate support to individuals who have sought assistance,” Enciso said.
He noted that victims are receiving legal consultations and guidance on the documentary requirements needed by UAE authorities.
“Given the ongoing consultations and the need to respect the desire of the individuals concerned to maintain confidentiality, we are unable to provide further details at this time,” he said.
PCG lawyer Eisa Khalife noted he is compiling evidence to formalize a case and may escalate the matter internationally.
“I may ask the Interpol (international police),” Khalife said, noting that he met with a delegation of 25 victims on October 7.
Interpol involvement would be required to extradite and bring the two suspects back to the UAE for prosecution.

Many victims paid for the steep visa fees by using up their personal savings or taking out high-interest loans from lending agencies. They became suspicious only after Trip Expert abruptly scrubbed its digital presence.
Cherry Laroga, an applicant, noticed the red flags when the company’s heavy stream of Facebook advertisements suddenly stopped.

“September 24 yung time na nag-scroll ako sa Facebook, ‘di na lumalabas ads nila. Duon ako nagtaka kaya naghanap ako sa TikTok, dun may nabasa akong comment na ‘wag bumili ng visa diyan kasi marami ang di na-process…kaya nag-message ako sa agent ko nung same day,” said Laroga.

(It was September 24 when I scrolled on Facebook and noticed that their ads were not showing anymore. I grew suspicious and searched TikTok, where I saw comments warning people not to buy visas from them because applications weren’t being processed. I messaged my agent that same day.)
She said her agent responded honestly.

“’I will be transparent with you, ma’am,’” Laroga said, recalling the agent’s response. “Wala daw pong funds ang company… kaya pati kaming empleyado walang sahod at hindi rin matapos ang application ninyo sa visa.’”
(The company reportedly has no funds…that’s why even us, employees, do not have salaries anymore, and it’s the reason why your visa application hasn’t been processed.)
The fallout quickly escalated across social media, prompting victims to storm Trip Expert’s abandoned corporate offices demanding refunds and report the incident to the PCG.
The victims are mostly domestic helpers, caregivers, and retail sales staff — who sought freelance visas to legally pursue independent, self-sponsored employment.
Gwendolyn Cajutol said she has accumulated more than AED11,000 in fines for overstaying because she still does not have her Emirates ID due to the scam.
“Fully paid na ko sa visa. Sakit ng naranasan ko ngayon. Masakit. Mahirap tanggapin po,” she said.
(I’ve already paid in full for the visa. What I’m going through right now is so painful. It hurts. It’s hard to accept.)
Fatima, who requested anonymity, said she had trusted the visa company because they were run by Filipinos. She had also felt assured by their regular social media advertisements.
“Noong una po, sila mismo ang sobrang kulit. Panay ang tawag at chat nila sa akin para kumbinsihin akong mag-avail ng kanilang self-sponsored visa processing,” she recalled.
(At first, they were the ones who were really persistent. They kept calling and messaging me to convince me to avail of their self-sponsored visa processing service.)
“Dahil mga kababayan ko rin po sila at mukhang maayos at legitimate ang kanilang operation, nagtiwala po ako,” Fatima said, adding that she paid AED9,000 in May this year.
“Binayaran ko po agad ng cash kasi sabi nila hindi daw ipa-process kapag hindi fully paid. Ang usapan po namin ay matatapos ang proseso within approximately 60 working days o dalawang buwan.”

(Since they are also my Filipinos and their operation seems to be sound and legitimate, I trusted them. I paid in cash immediately because they said the process wouldn’t move forward unless it was fully paid. We agreed that the process would be completed within approximately 60 working days, or two months.)
Fatima said things changed after she made the payment.

“Kung anu-anong dahilan na po ang sinasabi nila. Paulit-ulit nilang sinasabi na delayed daw sa authorities, kaya patuloy lang kaming naghihintay at umaasa. Ngayon po, magli-limang buwan na, pero wala pa rin akong residency visa,” she said.

(They kept giving all sorts of reasons. They repeatedly claimed that things were being delayed by the authorities, so we just kept waiting and hoping. It has now been nearly five months, yet I still do not have a residency visa.)
Her grace period has since expired, forcing her to exit the UAE to Oman twice on costly tourist visa extensions.
Fatima’s UAE bank account has also been frozen. She has been jobless for two months, and she cannot send money home to her family.

“Hindi na po ako halos makatulog. Hindi na ako makakain nang maayos dahil sa kakaisip kung ano ang mangyayari sa visa ko, sa pera ko at sa kinabukasan ko dito sa Dubai,” Fatima said, noting that she even borrowed the AED 9,000 needed to pay the visa fee.
(I can barely sleep or eat properly from worrying about my visa, my money, and my future in Dubai.)
“Kami po ang mga OFW na araw-araw nagtatrabaho at nagsasakripisyo para makaipon. Nagtiwala kami dahil mga kapwa Pilipino namin ang kausap namin,” added Fatima.
(We are OFWs who work and make sacrifices every single day in order to save money. We placed our trust in them) because we were dealing with fellow Filipinos.)

“Mas masakit po dahil sa ibang bansa na nga po kami, kapwa Pilipino pa sana ang aasahan namin. Kung sino pa ang kapwa Pilipino mo sa abroad, sila pa pala ang makakapagbigay sa ‘yo ng ganitong problema.”
“Gusto lang po namin ng hustisya.”

(It hurts even more because we’re already in a foreign country, so we’re expecting to be able to rely on fellow Filipinos. It turns out that the very people you’d expect to support you, your fellow Filipinos abroad, are the ones who end up causing you this kind of trouble. We just want justice.) – Rappler.com

articles.title: Sara Duterte can file charges vs witnesses in impeachment trial, says law professor
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte can file charges against the witnesses in her trial following the withdrawal of three articles of impeachment against her, a law professor said on Sunday.

blocks.text: Published October 18, 2026 8:53am
Vice President Sara Duterte can file charges against the witnesses in her trial following the withdrawal of three articles of impeachment against her, a law professor said on Sunday.

"Kung gusto ng Bise Presidente na i-vindicate ang kanyang sarili, maghain siya ng karampatang kaso sa mga tumestigo laban sa kanya, ito man perjury or violation ng confidentiality," said Adonis Gabriel of San Beda University College of Law in an interview with Super Radyo dzBB.
(If the Vice President wants to vindicate herself, she should file the appropriate charges against those who testified against her, whether it is perjury or violation of confidentiality.)
The Senate impeachment court earlier accepted the move by the House prosecution panel to withdraw three of the four Articles of Impeachment leveled against Duterte.

The prosecution said that it will no longer pursue three other charges against Duterte, saying its case will stand on Article II alone on alleged unexplained wealth due to non-full declaration of assets and non-divestment of business.
The Vice President can also charge the senator-judges if she wishes to, said Gabriel.
"Pwede maghain ng administrative case sa Senado mismo para tignan kung mayroong paglabag sa karapatan ng depensa ang mga huwes," he added.
(An administrative case can be filed right in the Senate to check if the judges violated the rights of the defense.)

Following the withdrawal of the three articles against her, Duterte's camp said the prosecution's withdrawal of three articles of impeachment on Tuesday is an admission that the allegations hurled against her lacked basis from the start.
"The withdrawal is an admission that the allegations lacked basis from the very beginning," said lawyer Salvador Paolo Panelo Jr. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: 'No Kings' rallies push early voting ahead of US midterm elections
articles.summary: Organizers of the "No Kings" protests, known for their anti-Trump sentiment, are urging Americans to vote early in the November 3 midterm elections, as Republicans face tough races to retain control…

image.caption: It was the fourth 'No Kings' protest since President Trump returned to officeImage: Madison Swart/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Protesters gathered across the United States for the latest "No Kings" demonstrations as Americans begin casting ballots ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.

Dubbed "No Kings: Vote Early," Saturday's event aimed to fire up Americans to vote early in the midterm elections, which will determine which party controls Congress, rather than protest against President Donald Trump and his administration.

"It's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard," organizers said in a statement.
Most areas of the United States allow voters to cast their ballots ahead of time, sometimes weeks in advance.

blocks.caption: There were more than 3,000 'No Kings' events planned across the USImage: Daniel Heuer/REUTERS

blocks.text: Trump opposes mail-in voting

Trump repeatedly criticized mail-in voting and sought to restrict the practice ahead of the midterms. He regularly votes by mail-in ballot, arguing that his job makes him an exception to his criticism of the practice.
The US president blamed election fraud, without providing evidence, for his defeat in the 2020 presidential election against Democrat Joe Biden.
Various surveys have concluded that restricting mail-in ballots could benefit Republicans, as Democratic voters disproportionately use the system to cast their ballots.
Opponents fear that the Trump administration may try to interfere with the midterm results, particularly if Republicans lose the majority.
Opinion polls suggest Democrats are poised to regain control of the House ​of Representatives, while the Senate remains too close to call.

articles.title: Ebike rider, 13, charged with sexual touching after girls and women allegedly harassed on northern beaches trails
articles.summary:
Sydney teenager charged with offensive behaviour and sexual touching without consent in relation to incidents involving females aged 13 to 54

An ebike riding 13-year-old boy has been charged…

blocks.text: An ebike riding 13-year-old boy has been charged with multiple sexual offences allegedly committed against women on walking trails on Sydney’s northern beaches.

New South Wales police said the boy was arrested on Saturday evening after a strike force was established to investigate inappropriate comments and alleged sexual touching incidents on walking trails in the Narrabeen area in the first weeks of October.
“Following a public appeal, a 13-year-old boy was arrested after attending Mona Vale police station about 7.30pm yesterday,” police said on Sunday.

The teenager was taken to Manly police station and charged with three counts of behaving in an offensive manner in or near a public place, and eight counts of sexually touching another person without consent.
On Saturday, police had released CCTV images of a male they believed could assist with inquiries.
Police allege that 11 separate incidents occurred against girls and women aged between 13 and 54.
The investigation was initially launched after three separate alleged incidents on 7 and 8 October.

“In each incident, a male allegedly approached women on walking trails, sexually touched them and then rode away on an ebike,” police said on Saturday. In one of the incidents, the offender allegedly made “inappropriate sexual comments”.
At Narrabeen lagoon about 4.30pm on 1 October the suspect “allegedly sexually touched [a] woman before riding away on an ebike,” police said.

Last Monday, police received a further report that between 5pm and 5.30pm that day, two women walking along the Narrabeen lagoon near Bilarong reserve had been sexually touched by a male riding an ebike.
Strike Force Mexvo was established to investigate the incidents with assistance from state crime command’s sex crimes quad.
Speaking in Narrabeen before Saturday’s arrest, Supt John Duncan urged members of the public to come forward with any information about the alleged incidents.
“It’s a bushland park that runs 8km, a large amount of which … runs through bushland, obviously there’s not a great deal of CCTV and cameras.”
The 13-year-old was granted conditional bail to appear at children’s court on 4 November.

articles.title: Arizona joins Nevada to fight proposed cuts to their shares of Colorado River
articles.summary:
Move comes after Trump administration announced restrictions that could slash water supplies

Arizona has joined Nevada in its legal battle against the Trump administration’s proposed cuts to…

blocks.text: Arizona has joined Nevada in its legal battle against the Trump administration’s proposed cuts to their shares of the shrinking Colorado River.

The move comes after the interior department announced restrictions this summer that could slash the water supplied to lower basin states – Arizona, California and Nevada – over the next two years depending on the river’s condition.
The river’s major reservoirs, Lake Mead and Lake Powell, have plummeted to historically low levels, due to overuse and a changing climate.

The states sharing the waterway were at an impasse with the upper basin states arguing that their downstream counterparts were responsible for the reservoir’s water shortages and should thus face the largest cuts.
The federal government’s intervention came after the states missed several deadlines for a consensus.
The fear looming over the state of the river is that if reservoir levels plunged far enough, the waterway would effectively not be able to flow downstream, a so-called deadpool.
The upper basin states – Wyoming, Colorado, Utah and New Mexico – were spared from the water cuts, an exemption that has drawn sharp rebuke from the leaders of the lower basin states.
“We are drawing a line in the sand,” Arizona governor Katie Hobbs said in a Friday statement.

“I am taking this legal action alongside Nevada because the federal government refuses to hold the Upper Basin accountable for the water deliveries they owe Arizona, and is threatening to force draconian cuts that go well beyond the Lower Basin Agreement,” Hobbs continued, referring to a two-year-voluntary water conservation pact among her state, California and Nevada.

Tom Buschatzke, the director of Arizona’s water department, said “intervention in the Nevada lawsuit is necessary at this time for Arizona to protect its legal rights to Colorado River water while preserving a path forward to achieving a collaborative outcome with California and Nevada to protect the Colorado River system”.
An interior department spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the joint litigation.

articles.title: Hurricane Trudy strengthens to category 2 as it heads toward Mexico
articles.summary:
Hurricane warning in effect from Manzanillo to Cabo Corrientes as storm moves toward Pacific coast

Trudy strengthened to a category 2 hurricane as it moved toward Mexico’s south-western and…

blocks.text: Trudy strengthened to a category 2 hurricane as it moved toward Mexico’s south-western and west-central Pacific coast on Saturday, the US National Hurricane Center said.

A hurricane warning was in effect from Manzanillo in Colima state to Cabo Corrientes in Jalisco. The latest NHC data showed Trudy with maximum sustained winds of 100mph (155km/h) and about 205 miles (330km) south/south-east of Cabo Corrientes and 115 miles (180km) south/south-west of Manzanillo, moving north-west at 10mph (17km/h).
Meanwhile, Typhoon Champi strengthened into a category 4 weather system as it moved toward Guam.

Trudy’s center was expected to approach the Mexican coast on Saturday and pass near it into Sunday. After the latest warning, Mexico’s government issued a tropical storm warning for Las Islas Marias and discontinued a similar warning for its coast south of Lazaro Cardenas.
The Mexican navy urged mariners and coastal residents to exercise extreme caution because of high waves, heavy rain and the risk of rising rivers, flooding and landslides in vulnerable areas.
Colima authorities said the risks remained low, but warned that heavy rainfall could cause damage because the ground was already saturated by successive storms along the Pacific coast.
Trudy was expected to bring 4-8in (10-20cm) of rain through the weekend, with isolated totals of about 15in (38cm).
Also in the Pacific, Champi strengthened into a category 4 storm as it moved west toward Guam at 15mph (24km/h).
By Saturday night local time, Champi was about 25 miles (40km) south-east of Guam, with maximum sustained winds of 140mph (225km/h), according to the US National Weather Service.

The storm was forecast to pass south of Guam early Sunday local time and continue intensifying through the day. Guam and Rota remained under a typhoon warning, while Tinian and Saipan were under a tropical storm warning and typhoon watch.

The governors of Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands both requested emergency disaster declarations on Friday. Approval by Donald Trump would authorize federal support and funding for emergency protective measures.

Airports, harbors and some health facilities in the territories were closed. Resources were unlikely to reach the islands for three to five days, according to Saturday updates from the Federal Emergency Management Agency.
The territories are still recovering from Super Typhoons Sinlaku and Bavi, which struck in April and July, respectively.

articles.title: Two people, including child, killed after person drives through soccer game in Kansas
articles.summary:
The driver of the vehicle is in custody, and two juveniles were in the vehicle, according to Wichita police department

Two people, including a child, were killed during a soccer game in…

blocks.text: Two people, including a child, were killed during a soccer game in Wichita, Kansas, when a person drove a vehicle through the field at Stryker soccer complex, police have confirmed. Multiple other people were injured.
The driver of the vehicle is in custody, Aaron Moses of the Wichita police department said Saturday in a news conference. There were two juveniles in the vehicle, he said.

Police confirmed that one child was killed at the scene and one adult was killed, but did not release any names or ages until family could be notified. “This is a tragedy,” Moses said. Those injured were taken to hospitals but the extent of their injuries is unknown.
Moses said he did not know how fast the vehicle was traveling or how it got onto the field.
Officials are still investigating and the city has said all events at the soccer complex are canceled until further notice.

A witness told local news station KWCH that a black pickup truck was seen “plowing through the youth soccer fields”. The truck hit multiple people before stopping 100-200 yards down the fields, the witness said. They reported seeing dozens of emergency responders giving aid and CPR to the victims.
